newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk c.bank lifts money rates amid inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: Turk c.bank lifts money rates amid inflation fears.

text.p: The Turkish central bank raised its money market rates on Wednesday amid fears of higher inflation, aggravated by official remarks that end-year inflation could reach around 100 percent.
The central bank raised its overnight money, tomorrow/next and tomorrow/week bid and offer rates by one to two percentage points at the opening.

Bankers said the central bank's move, which had been expected, followed State Minister Gunes Taner's remarks that inflation would reach around 100 percent by the end of 1997. His three-week-old government only recently revised its end-year forecast to 85 percent.
"As a result, inflation began to rise rapidly and we think the trend will continue and year-end inflation will be around 100 percent," Taner told Reuters in an interview.
The central bank raised its overnight rates by two pct points to 54-74 pct from 52-72 percent. It also raised tom/next rates to 55-73 percent from 54-71 and the tom/week offer rate to 74 pct from 72.

"Although the market was expecting the central bank to raise money market rates because of rising cost of funding in the bond market, the minister's words on inflation were a surprise for us," said a private bank treasurer.
The lira firmed to 156,910 per dollar from its opening of 157,100 but later fell to 157,200 from 156,310 on Tuesday.
Bond rates jumped more than seven points because of the higher inflation expectations. The most active May 13, 1997 paper jumped 7.6 points to 119.09 percent from 111.50 at Tuesday's close.
The consumer inflation rate was 78 percent in June.
The market opened 60.1 trillion lira short on Wednesday and the central bank opened a seven-day repo auction to meet the demand for cash from banks. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
